title: Multi-omics Analysis of CLSPN in Cancer Prognosis and Drug Resistance
author: Chen, Wen, et al.
materials: The 4 μm paraffin-embedded lung adenocarcinoma tissue sections were blocked with 3% H2O2 and 3% BSA after undergoing dewaxing, hydration and antigen retrieval. Multiplexed immunofluorescence staining of Claspin (Rabbit, 1:200, abcam, UK), CD8 (Rabbit, 1:400, CST, USA), PD-1 (Rabbit, 1:200, abcam, UK) and PD-L1 (Rabbit, 1:100, abcam, UK) were performed according to the manufacturer's instructions (AiFang biological, 6-Color Multiple fluorescence Kit, China). The images were captured using AKOYA multispectral microscope.

Transient plasmid transfection was conducted in accordance with the Lipofectamine 3000 reagent instruction (Invitrogen, USA). shRNA targeting CLSPN (sh-CLSPN) and its negative control shRNA (NC) were constructed by GeneChem. After cultured for 48 h, cells mRNA and protein were extracted to validate transfection efficiency.

steps.title: Collect pan‑cancer multi‑omics datasets
steps.instruction: Download transcriptomic, epigenomic and pharmacogenomics data for 9 125 tumor samples covering 33 cancer types from public repositories to create an integrated pan‑cancer dataset.

steps.title: Analyze CLSPN expression with online tools
steps.instruction: Use TIMER2 (http://timer.cistrome.org/) and GEPIA2 (http://gepia2.cancer-pku.cn/#analysis) to obtain CLSPN expression levels; validate expression in cell lines with CCLE (https://portals.broadinstitute.org/ccle/); transform raw TPM values to log2(TPM + 1) for box‑plot generation.

steps.title: Perform survival analyses in R
steps.instruction: Run univariate Cox regression for overall survival (OS), disease‑specific survival (DSS), disease‑free interval (DFI) and progression‑free interval (PFI) across all TCGA cancers; generate Kaplan–Meier curves with the R packages “survminer” and “survival”; consider P < 0.05 as statistically significant.

steps.title: Retrieve CLSPN alteration data from cBioPortal
steps.instruction: Access https://www.cbioportal.org/, use the “cancer types summary” module to obtain alteration frequency, mutation type and copy‑number alteration (CNA) for all TCGA tumors; use the “comparison” module to extract OS, DFS, PFS and DSS data for cases with and without CLSPN alterations.

steps.title: Estimate tumor stromal and immune scores
steps.instruction: Apply the ESTIMATE algorithm via the R packages “estimate” and “limma” to compute Immune score, Stromal score and ESTIMATE score for each tumor sample; store results for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Assess immune infiltration with deconvolution
steps.instruction: Run XCELL and CIBERSORT on the expression matrix to quantify immune cell fractions across cancer types.

steps.title: Correlate CLSPN with checkpoint, TMB and MSI
steps.instruction: Obtain immune‑checkpoint marker levels; evaluate tumor mutational burden (TMB) and microsatellite instability (MSI) scores using the UCSCxenashiny tool; compute Spearman correlations between CLSPN expression and each metric.

steps.title: Correlate CLSPN with MMR genes and methylation
steps.instruction: Perform Spearman correlation between CLSPN and five MMR genes (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2, EPCAM) and four DNA methyltransferases (DNMT1, DNMT2, DNMT3A, DNMT3B) in each cancer type; conduct Kaplan–Meier survival analysis of CLSPN methylation status (P < 0.05); explore single‑CpG effects with MethSurv (https://biit.cs.ut.ee/methsurv/) and generate heatmaps via the “Gene visualization” tab.

steps.title: Conduct Gene Set Enrichment Analysis
steps.instruction: Download CLSPN‑related expression data from cBioPortal; run GSEA using the R packages “fgsea” and “ggplot2” to identify enriched pathways; visualize results.

steps.title: Prepare multiplex immunofluorescence on lung tissue
steps.instruction: Section paraffin‑embedded lung adenocarcinoma blocks at 4 µm; dewax, rehydrate and perform antigen retrieval; block sections with 3 % H₂O₂ and 3 % BSA; stain simultaneously with the following primary antibodies diluted as indicated: Claspin (Rabbit, 1:200, Abcam, UK), CD8 (Rabbit, 1:400, CST, USA), PD‑1 (Rabbit, 1:200, Abcam, UK), PD‑L1 (Rabbit, 1:100, Abcam, UK) using the AiFang Biological 6‑Color Multiple Fluorescence Kit (China) according to the manufacturer’s protocol; capture images on an AKOYA multispectral microscope.

steps.title: Culture human lung cell lines
steps.instruction: Obtain BEAS‑2B (normal pulmonary epithelium) and lung cancer lines H1299, Calu‑3, SPCA1, HCC827, PC9, A549 from the Institutes of Biomedical Sciences (Shanghai, China); maintain cells in either DMEM or RPMI‑1640 supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum (FBS) at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Transiently transfect cells with sh‑CLSPN plasmid
steps.instruction: Prepare Lipofectamine 3000 transfection complexes according to the Invitrogen (USA) protocol; transfect cells with shRNA targeting CLSPN (sh‑CLSPN) or negative‑control shRNA (NC) plasmids constructed by GeneChem; incubate for 48 h; harvest cells for RNA and protein extraction to verify knock‑down efficiency.

steps.title: Isolate RNA and perform RT‑qPCR
steps.instruction: Lyse cells with Trizol reagent (AG RNAex Pro Reagent, China) and extract total RNA; reverse‑transcribe RNA into cDNA following the kit instructions; set up SYBR Green qPCR reactions using SYBR Green Pro Taq HS Premix (China); use the following primer pairs (5'‑3'): CLSPN F TGGAGAGTGGGGTCCATTCAT / R CCGGGGTTTACGTTTGAAGAAA; CCNA2 F GGTACTGAAGTCCGGGAACC / R TGCTTTCCAAGGAGGAACGG; CCNB1 F GCACTTCCTTCGGAGAGCAT / R TTCTTAGCCAGGTGCTGCAT; CCNB2 F GCGTGCCATCCTAGTGGATT / R AGCTTCTTCCGGGAAACTGG; CCNE2 F TCACTGATGGTGCTTGCAGT / R GTAAAATGGCACAAGGCAGCA; CDK1 F CTGGGGTCAGCTCGTTACTC / R TCCACTTCTGGCCACACTTC; CDK2 F GCTTTTGGAGTCCCTGTTCG / R GCGAGTCACCATCTCAGCAA; CDK4 F TGAAATTGGTGTCGGTGCCT / R ACCTTGATCTCCCGGTCAGT; CDK6 F ACAGAGCACCCGAAGTCTTG / R CTGGGAGTCCAATCACGTCC; ACTIN F CCTGGCACCCAGCACAAT / R GGGCCGGACTCGTCATAC.

steps.title: Analyze cell cycle by flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Resuspend harvested cells in 1 ml DNA Staining solution and add 10 µl Permeabilization solution (MULTI SCIENCES, Zhejiang, China); incubate at room temperature for 30 min; acquire data on a flow cytometer and analyze cell‑cycle distribution.

steps.title: Download drug sensitivity data from CellMiner
steps.instruction: Access the CellMiner™ database (https://discover.nci.nih.gov/cellminer/); retrieve drug concentration (IC₅₀) values and corresponding CLSPN expression profiles for all available cancer cell lines.

steps.title: Correlate CLSPN expression with drug sensitivity
steps.instruction: Compute Spearman correlations between CLSPN expression and IC₅₀ values; note positive associations with PF‑06463922, salinomycin, KU‑55933, Olaparib, AZD‑3463, etc., and negative associations with Birinapant, 6‑Thioguanine, and Nelarabine (P < 0.05).

steps.title: Run Connectivity Map analysis for candidate drugs
steps.instruction: Perform differential expression analysis between CLSPN‑high and CLSPN‑low samples in TCGA‑LUAD, SKCM, COAD, BRCA, CESC, PRAD and PAAD; select the 300 most significant DEGs (top 150 up‑regulated and top 150 down‑regulated); submit the gene list to the CMap website (https://clue.io) for each corresponding cell line; retrieve CMap scores for darifenacin and eltrombopag; interpret negative scores as potential therapeutic efficacy for CLSPN‑high groups.

steps.title: Molecular docking of candidate drugs to CHK1‑Claspin complex
steps.instruction: Download the CHK1 kinase domain‑Claspin phosphopeptide structure (PDB ID: 7ako); prepare protein and ligand files; use AutoDockTools to dock darifenacin, dihydroergotamine, netupitan, fosaprepitant and eltrombopag; record binding energies (‑8.9, ‑8.8, ‑8.8, ‑8.4, ‑8.4 kcal/mol respectively); visualize binding modes with PyMOL and generate 2‑D interaction diagrams.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis of experimental data
steps.instruction: Analyze survival curves with log‑rank test; compute Spearman or Pearson correlations as appropriate; compare two groups with Student’s t‑test and multiple groups with one‑way ANOVA; consider P < 0.05 as significant.

description: Claspin was discovered as an adaptor or scaffold protein necessary for Chk1 activation in response to DNA replication blocks and stalled replication forks [2]. Previous researches reported that the repetitive phosphopeptide motif in human Claspin was important for Claspin-Chk1 interaction to mediate Claspin function [34, 35]. Considering that Claspin acted as a scaffold protein facilitating the recruitment of CHK1 into larger complexes, we used the structure of CHK1 kinase domain and Claspin phosphopeptide complex (PDB ID:7ako) for molecular docking to screen related FDA-approved drugs. The results indicated that the drugs bound to the complex of Claspin phosphopeptide and CHK1 mainly through strong electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions (Fig. 11A-E). The first five drugs with the lowest binding energy were Darifenacin, Dihydroergotamine, Netupitan, Fosaprepitant and Eltrombopag. The binding energy were − 8.9 kcal/mol, − 8.8 kcal/mol, − 8.8 kcal/mol, − 8.4 kcal/mol, − 8.4 kcal/mol indicating a highly stable binding. We performed CMap analysis to validate the drugs predicted by molecular docking, which indicated that eltrombopag might serve as a potential therapeutic drug in SKCM patients with highly expressed CLSPN, and darifenacin might act as potential therapeutic drug in PRAD, CESC, BRCA, COAD, LUAD, PAAD patients with CLSPN high expression (Fig. 11F).Fig. 11Validation of the affinity of the candidate drugs by molecular docking analysis and CMap analysis. D Binding mode of the protein complex and Fosaprepitant. E Binding mode of the protein complex and Eltrombopag.
